findings.what: forDisplay runs JSON.parse then JSON.stringify, so the drawer shows the API's money tokens changed: 803.40 shows as 803.4, 500.00 as 500, and a 0.00 refund as 0.
findings.why: WB-7 asks for 'the exact request and response of every action'. The API deliberately writes every decimal to at least two places (src/Uinsure.Policies.Api/Contracts/TwoDecimalPlacesConverter.cs:7-29, '803.40, not 803.4'). Sending the response through JS numbers drops those zeros, so the inspector shows a body the API never sent. That is worst on COULD-2 £0 refunds and any amount with a zero in the pence. Acceptance 4 asks for indented JSON, not re-serialised values, and keeping the log's wire text exact doesn't help because the display is what the user reads. The indenting has to keep the received tokens as they were (whitespace changes only).

findings.what: No test checks that the indented body keeps the API's tokens. Every amount used has non-zero pence, and leaves() compares String(parsed) by substring, so 803.4 passes against 803.40.
findings.why: The e2e tests (wb-7.spec.ts:10086-10120 in the packet; amounts 611.29, 633.41, 602.17, 644.52, 538.26) and the unit test only check indentation and parsed leaves. String(803.4) is a substring of both '803.4' and '803.40', so the suite passes whether R1 is present or fixed. That breaks the requirements-trace rule that a test written from a finding must fail before the fix. A red test is needed: a recorded or stubbed response whose raw text holds a value like 803.40 or 0.00, asserting the drawer's text contains that exact token.
